name: Every persona signs in with the password the input names, also a user a layer copy delivered

dependsOn.why: The users are that recipe's objects; this one only makes each sign in with its own password, which create_users sets only on create.

mcpOnly.reason: No MCP tool sets a password on an existing user: update_users has no password member (0.6.6 refuses one), so the password step needs the Management API command UserSetPassword.

hosted.reason: The sign-in is a delivery API read and UserSetPassword a Management API command; nothing needs SQL or a recycle.

steps.title: Find each user that has a password reference
steps.trap: A user name can exist twice (one person on two accounts, a layer copy's second profile): two matches block the item rather than set a password on the wrong one.

steps.title: Set the password a user does not sign in with

bindings.reason: No MCP tool sets a password on an existing user: create_users takes one on create only and update_users has no password member (MCP 0.6.6 answers unknown member users[0].password).

steps.trap: The find is a sign-in with the input's password: a user who signs in is left alone, so a run never rotates a working password. UserSetPassword keys on userId, not id, and the Management API UserSave accepts a password and drops it. Never copy a hash through SQL, and never delete and recreate the user: its id changes and every order, price and grant that names it breaks.

probes.title: Each user with a password signs in through the delivery API

provenOn.evidence: on a site built from empty by the recipe set, with one more user that existed without the input's password (as a layer copy ships it): p1-verify reported that user WOULD-CREATE and the two personas users.accounts created UNCHANGED (5 of 7, the sign-in probe failing on that user), p2-apply set its password with UserSetPassword and read it back as a sign-in (7 of 7), p3-verify and p4-apply-again 7 of 7 with nothing written. update_users with a password member was refused on 0.6.6 (unknown member users[0].password).

traps: A layer copy ships its personas without a password; this recipe gives each the password the input names by reference, after users.accounts and with no debt: authentication reads the stored password on every attempt.
A recipe set on a blank site creates the users with their password in users.accounts, so this recipe finds every persona signing in and writes nothing.
